$comment: The cut of the demo video. Source of truth for voice-over text, on-screen labels and timing; docs/submission/demo-video-script.md is the owner-facing description of the same shots (tests/video-kit.test.js checks they agree). Segments say which part of which recorded scene plays, at what speed. 'maxSeconds' compresses a long wait to at most that long and the assembler labels it 'Sped up xN, real time shown' with a real-time clock. Marks are the names the recorder writes into scratch/video/clips/<scene>.json.

shots.title: Title
shots.label: XRPL Testnet · no real value
shots.vo: This is ResearchAgent: research with a wallet. It pays writers for the articles it's missing, inside your budget, on the XRP Ledger.

shots.title: The live sandbox: ask, plan, pay
shots.label: {scenes.hosted-ask.labels.caption}
shots.vo: Open the link, ask a question, set a budget. A five-second plan shows what it will do: free sources first, then at most one article per round. A model recommends what to buy, but only policy code can pay. Each payment sits in a native XRPL escrow, and the writer is paid by publishing the article's key on the ledger.

shots.title: Refund and key reveal, on the ledger
shots.label: Replay of a recorded Testnet run · fictional writers · no backend
shots.vo: Here's the key, on the ledger, in the fulfilment. Delivery and payment are one event. This article broke its promise, so the writer signed a refund and its trust score dropped. A real writer could refuse; then the buyer keeps a fraud proof anyone can check.

segments.label: XRPL Testnet · the Fulfillment is the article key · no real value
Refund is writer-signed: our fixture writer cooperates; a real writer could refuse · replay of a recorded Testnet run · fictional writers

shots.title: It can say no, and prove it
shots.label: {scenes.hosted-decline.labels.caption}
shots.vo: It can also say no. Here no source covered the question, so it bought nothing, and the refusal is anchored on XRPL Testnet. Anyone can open the proof page and check it.

shots.title: The same product inside Claude Code (MCP)
shots.label: Claude Code over MCP · XRPL Testnet · no real value · team-authored writer · real content · not an independent writer
shots.vo: Any agent can use it. Claude Code adds it with one line, and the spending caps live in the environment, where the model can't raise them. Ask about XRPL and it buys from our own build notes, labelled as ours, and answers with citations and ledger links.

shots.title: Don't trust us, verify it
shots.label: Python verifier · no Node · read-only XRPL Testnet lookups
shots.vo: Don't trust us. A Python verifier, written separately from our TypeScript one, re-checks every receipt against the ledger. Our ledger page re-validates every recorded transaction from your browser.

segments.label: {facts.transactions} Testnet transactions · checked live from your browser · no real value

shots.title: One line, no clone: try --testnet
shots.label: XRPL Testnet · no real value · fixture models · fictional writers
shots.vo: For builders: one line, no clone, no account. It buys, catches a broken promise, gets refunded, re-buys, anchors the answer and verifies all six transactions against the ledger.

shots.title: Builder feedback and honest limits
shots.label: {facts.feedback_line}
shots.vo: We wrote down what fought us: seven ranked findings, each with a script that reproduces it. The top one: the RLUSD issuer lacks the flag token escrow needs, so we use a labelled Testnet token. Mainnet is a checklist, not a claim.

shots.title: Close
shots.label: github.com/Collaboration95/theFastandtheFungible · XRPL Testnet only · no real value
shots.vo: ResearchAgent. An open market where agents pay the people who know, and the ledger keeps everyone honest. Thank you.
